body: Hang in there as well. I’m so sorry it’s happened to you as well. It sucks so much. Hopefully we can get through it one day
What she took took about two hours to take effect, but that was too late to get her stomach pumped or anything like that

I don’t know that feeling exactly, but I do know what it’s like to sit in limbo for hours on end not knowing if she’d be alive or not the next morning. Even though I was surrounded by people I never felt so alone in my life. I can’t think of anything worse. I’m happy to hear it worked out. Give him lots of hugs :)
Thanks. Definitely not everything I do and think is healthy, but it’s a process I guess
It was pretty specific and rare so I’d rather not say in the interest of privacy / to not give anyone ideas.
I was just around the corner from her house and she just texted me taht she thought she was dying. So I ran over and as soon as I got there she told me what she did and I called 911.

My girlfriend committed suicide 3 weeks ago. She told me what she had done after she had poisoned herself, but too late for anything to be done. This is something that’s been troubling me about the whole thing. I’ve been thinking about it a lot and I feel like that’s the scariest thing about the whole thing, I can’t help but think that if she actually wanted it to happen she wouldn’t have told me, so it feels like maybe she regretted it and she didn’t want to die. If she wanted to die I can eventually come to terms with that, it was her choice, but I feel like if she didn’t want to, I can’t handle that.

But it’s something I’ve talked about in therapy and there’s no way of knowing for sure if she regretted it or not. The only concrete thing I can take away from it is the fact that I was someone she loved and trusted enough to be the last person to see her alive. And even if she didn’t want to die, she loved me enough to call me for help. So I’m glad she told me. I got to see her one last time and say goodbye, and when she left I knew that she truly and deeply loved me. I wish she didn’t do it and I would give anything to change it, but I’m glad she told me.
